knowledge:
- key_parameters: EXP=A matrix of gene expression data where rows represent genes and columns represent samples ;; trait=A matrix of external traits (e.g., clinical data or miRNA) where rows represent traits and columns represent samples (required for supervised analysis) ;; measure=The similarity metric to use, either "MI" (mutual information) or "corr" (correlation) ;; nflag=An integer flag indicating the analysis type: 1 for Unsupervised (gene-gene) or 2 for Supervised (gene-trait) ;; net.trim=The network trimming method from the minet package (e.g., "aracne", "mrnet", "clr") used when measure is "MI" ;; n.replica=The number of permutations to perform for p-value calculation (default is 400) ;; thresh=The significance threshold used to filter associations for predicting the network ;; method.permut=An integer flag (1, 2, or 3) indicating the permutation correction method for multiple hypothesis testing in supervised analysis
- alternatives: minet=The underlying package used for mutual information computation and network trimming (mrnet/clr/aracne) ;; cor/cor.test=R built-in functions used for correlation-based similarity and exact p-value calculations
- when_to_use: Use when you want to construct gene co-expression/association networks (unsupervised) or associate gene expression profiles with clinical/external traits (supervised) using either correlation or mutual information, with robust permutation-based p-value correction.
- pitfalls: High computational cost: Supervised analysis with correction for both genes and traits can be slow (e.g., 2 minutes for a small 50x12 matrix) ;; Correlation limitations: When correlation ("corr") is used, only exact p-values are output, and some permutation-based multiple testing corrections are not applicable.

workflows.name: unsupervised_gene_association
workflows.intent: Compute similarity and predict interaction networks among genes (unsupervised analysis) using mutual information.
input: expression_matrix.csv (tabular gene expression data where rows are genes and columns are samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the expression data and format it as a matrix ;; 2. Run the BUS wrapper function with nflag=1 (unsupervised), specifying the similarity measure, network trimming method, and significance threshold ;; 3. Extract the similarity matrix, single/multiple permutation p-values, and the predicted network.
workflows.code:
library(BUS)
library(minet)
data(copasi)
mat=as.matrix(copasi)[1:5,]
rownames(mat)<-paste("G",1:nrow(mat), sep="")
BUS(EXP=mat,measure="MI",n.replica=400,net.trim="aracne",thresh=0.05,nflag=1)

workflows.name: supervised_gene_trait_association
workflows.intent: Compute similarity and identify associations between genes and external traits (supervised analysis) using mutual information.
input: trait_matrix.csv (tabular external trait data, e.g., clinical or miRNA profiles, where columns match the expression samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the gene expression data and external trait data, formatting both as matrices with matching columns (samples) ;; 2. Run the BUS wrapper function with nflag=2 (supervised), specifying the similarity measure ;; 3. Extract the similarity matrix and single/multiple permutation p-values.
workflows.code:
data(tumors.mRNA)
exp<- as.matrix(tumors.mRNA)[11:15,]
rownames(exp)<-rownames(tumors.mRNA)[11:15]
data(tumors.miRNA)
trait<- as.matrix(tumors.miRNA)[11:15,]
rownames(trait)<-rownames(tumors.miRNA)[11:15]
BUS(EXP=exp,trait=trait,measure="MI",nflag=2)
